summary: Validated P0 Listing Promotion / Boost Payment System. Backend: 11/11 ran tests pass via pytest against the public preview URL (1 storage-sort test naturally skipped — DB has 0 storage auctions). All 3 tier prices match spec ($12.14 / $29.90 / $59.51 grand totals); validation errors return 400; non-owner returns 403; storage_type+marketplace_id returns 404; admin /admin/promotions endpoints (active list, social-share-queue, revenue summary) all return 200 with expected schema; promoted-first sort verified on /api/listings. Frontend: logged in as admin, opened /listing/{sample}, clicked the 'Promote This Listing' button (data-testid=promote-listing-btn), modal opened (data-testid=promote-listing-modal) with all three tier cards (tier-basic, tier-standard, tier-premium); selecting Standard renders promotion-breakdown with promo-stripe-fee-row and promo-grand-total = $29.90 CAD (matches backend within the documented ~$0.04 cosmetic single-pass variance). StorageAuctionDetail.js confirmed via code-grep to mount the modal with listingType='storage' and a button data-testid='boost-storage-auction-btn' (live UI exercise skipped — 0 storage auctions in DB).

action_items: Optional cosmetic alignment: the modal preview uses single-pass gross-up while the backend uses two-pass — preview shows ~$0.04 less than the actual charge. Acceptable per main-agent note; could be aligned by serving the breakdown via an existing /api/fees/estimate-style endpoint or by switching the modal to two-pass math.

Seed at least one storage auction so the storage-promotion sort and the boost-storage-auction-btn UI flow can be exercised end-to-end in a future iteration (currently /api/storage-auctions returns 0 items and the test naturally skips).
Live Stripe is in cs_live_* mode in this preview env — never click 'Pay' inside the modal; verification is limited to checkout_url generation and metadata.
critical_code_review_comments: payments_promotions.py: tier pricing constants (9.99 / 24.99 / 49.99) and tax rates (5% GST, 9.975% QST) appear hard-coded in the route — consider centralising into pricing_manager.py alongside the other gross-up logic so future tier changes only touch one file.
payments_promotions.py: legacy POST /payments/promote is preserved 'just in case' but is now dead code from the FE side. Add a deprecation log + 90-day removal plan to avoid two-endpoint drift.

admin_ops.py /admin/promotions endpoints: ensure the listing_title + seller_name enrichment uses a single $lookup or batched fetch — N+1 query patterns will hurt the active-promotions table once the queue grows.

scheduled_jobs.process_expired_promotions: confirm there is an idempotency guard (e.g., only update docs where promotion_end <= now AND is_promoted == true) so a missed cron tick doesn't double-write.

Frontend ListingPromotionModal: the cosmetic ~$0.04 mismatch between preview and backend is acceptable but worth a small UI note ('final amount confirmed at checkout') so users aren't surprised — confirm this disclaimer is present in both EN and FR.

rca_of_the_issue: Originally the Promote button returned 405 Method Not Allowed because the FE was POSTing to a path that no longer existed after a route refactor. Main agent's fix introduced a canonical POST /api/payments/promote-listing handler in payments_promotions.py with full pricing breakdown (base + 5% GST + 9.975% QST on base, then two-pass Stripe gross-up for 2.9% + $0.30 domestic). Verified live: basic returns grand_total $12.14, standard $29.90, premium $59.51 — slightly higher than the spec-approximate $11.83 / $29.56 / $59.15 because the two-pass gross-up additionally covers the Stripe fee on the taxes themselves (which the single-pass approximation in the spec did not). This is correct revenue math — the ~$0.30 difference at the premium tier is the seller-revenue protection. No remaining defects.
